say: The airline told her the bag was safe. Her AirTag showed it at a random apartment complex.
show: The *airline* told her the bag was *safe.* Her AirTag showed it at a [random apartment complex.]

say: But the AirTag didn't find it. A stranger's phone did.
show: But the AirTag *didn't* find it. A [stranger's phone] did.

say: An AirTag has no GPS. No SIM. No Wi-Fi. It talks over Bluetooth, on a coin battery.
show: An AirTag has *no GPS.* No SIM. No Wi-Fi. It talks over *Bluetooth,* on a [coin battery.]

say: Over and over, it whispers one thing: I'm here.
show: Over and over, it *whispers* one thing: [I'm here.]

say: Any nearby iPhone hears it, even yours. It adds its own location, locks it, and sends it to Apple.
show: Any nearby *iPhone* hears it, [even yours.] It adds its *own location,* locks it, and [sends it to Apple.]

say: Then her phone downloads that report, unlocks it, and there's her bag.

say: Only she holds the key. Apple can't read the location, and the stranger can't see whose tag it is.

say: Now repeat that across hundreds of millions of Apple devices. That's how a twenty-nine dollar disc knew more than the airline.

say: And to stop stalkers: if an unknown AirTag travels with you, your phone can warn you. iPhone or Android.
